statement: Lightning never strikes the same place twice.
fact: Lightning often strikes the same place repeatedly. The Empire State Building is hit about 20 to 25 times every year.

statement: Humans use only 10% of their brains.
fact: Brain imaging shows that we use virtually all of our brain, just not all regions at the same moment. Even during sleep, many areas stay active.

statement: The Great Wall of China is easily visible to the naked eye from the Moon.
fact: The wall is long but very narrow, and astronauts have confirmed it cannot be seen from the Moon. It is barely visible even from low Earth orbit.

statement: Goldfish have a memory span of only three seconds.
fact: Studies show goldfish can remember things for months. They can even be trained to respond to specific sounds and colors.

statement: Bats are blind.
fact: All bat species can see, and some see quite well. Many also use echolocation to navigate in the dark.

statement: Water flows down the drain in opposite directions in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.
fact: The Coriolis effect is far too weak to influence water in a sink. The direction depends on the basin's shape and how the water was disturbed.

statement: The tongue has separate zones for sweet, sour, salty and bitter tastes.
fact: The 'tongue map' is a myth caused by a mistranslated study. All taste types can be detected across the whole tongue.

statement: Napoleon Bonaparte was unusually short for his time.
fact: Napoleon was about 5 feet 6 or 7 inches, average or slightly above for a Frenchman of his era. The myth came from confusion between French and English units and British propaganda.

statement: Mount Everest is the tallest mountain on Earth when measured from base to peak.
fact: Mauna Kea in Hawaii is taller from its base on the ocean floor. Everest is only the highest above sea level.

statement: Sharks can get cancer.
fact: Sharks do develop cancer, including tumors in their cartilage. The idea that they are immune is a myth that fueled harmful supplement sales.

statement: Honey never spoils.
fact: Its low moisture and acidic nature make it hostile to bacteria. Edible honey has been found in ancient Egyptian tombs.

statement: A day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus.
fact: Venus takes about 243 Earth days to rotate once but only about 225 Earth days to orbit the Sun.

statement: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid of Giza.
fact: The Great Pyramid was built around 2560 BCE, about 2,500 years before Cleopatra lived. The Moon landing happened about 2,000 years after her.

statement: Humans have five senses and only five.
fact: People also have senses such as balance, temperature, pain and proprioception, which is awareness of body position. The five-sense idea dates back to Aristotle.

statement: Bulls are enraged by the color red.
fact: Bulls are dichromats and cannot distinguish red well. They react to the movement of the cape, not its color.

statement: The Sahara is the largest desert in the world.
fact: Antarctica is the largest desert because deserts are defined by low precipitation, not heat. The Sahara is the largest hot desert.

statement: Octopuses have three hearts.
fact: Two hearts pump blood through the gills and one circulates it to the rest of the body. Their blood is also blue because it uses copper-based hemocyanin.

statement: Ostriches bury their heads in the sand when scared.
fact: Ostriches don't do this. When threatened they run quickly or lie flat on the ground, which may look like hiding from far away.

statement: Bananas grow on trees.
fact: Banana plants are giant herbs. What looks like a trunk is actually a stack of tightly wrapped leaf stalks.

statement: Glass is a slow-moving liquid, which is why old windows are thicker at the bottom.
fact: Glass is an amorphous solid and does not flow at room temperature. Old panes are uneven because of how they were manufactured.

statement: The capital of Australia is Sydney.
fact: The capital is Canberra, which was purpose-built as a compromise between rivals Sydney and Melbourne.

statement: Russia spans more than ten time zones.
fact: Russia covers eleven time zones, more than any other country except France when its overseas territories are counted.

statement: Alaska is the largest US state by area.
fact: Alaska covers about 665,000 square miles, more than twice the size of Texas, the second largest.

statement: Africa has more countries than any other continent.
fact: Africa has 54 recognized sovereign countries, the most of any continent.

statement: The Amazon is the longest river in the world by most modern measurements.
fact: The Nile has traditionally been considered longest, though some recent measurements argue for the Amazon. Most sources still list the Nile at about 6,650 km.

statement: Canada has more lakes than the rest of the world's countries combined.
fact: Canada contains a majority of the world's lakes, estimated at over 2 million, thanks to glaciation during the last Ice Age.

statement: Mount Kilimanjaro is located in Kenya.
fact: Kilimanjaro is in Tanzania, though it is visible from parts of southern Kenya. It is the highest mountain in Africa.

statement: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world by area.
fact: At about 0.44 square kilometers, Vatican City is smaller than most city parks and is an independent state within Rome.

statement: The Dead Sea is a sea in the strict geographical sense.
fact: The Dead Sea is actually a landlocked salt lake. It is also one of the saltiest bodies of water on Earth.

statement: Nepal's national flag is not rectangular.
fact: Nepal's flag is made of two stacked pennants and is the only national flag in the world that is not a quadrilateral.

statement: Istanbul is the capital of Turkey.
fact: Ankara is Turkey's capital. Istanbul is the largest city and was the capital of the Ottoman Empire.

statement: Greenland is bigger than Africa.
fact: Africa is about 14 times larger than Greenland. Mercator maps stretch areas near the poles and make Greenland look enormous.

statement: Chile is one of only two countries in South America that does not border Brazil.
fact: Chile and Ecuador are the only two South American countries without a border with Brazil.

statement: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean on Earth.
fact: The Pacific covers about a third of the planet's surface and contains the Mariana Trench, the deepest known point in the ocean.

statement: Lightning is hotter than the surface of the Sun.
fact: A lightning bolt can heat the air to about 30,000 K, roughly five times hotter than the Sun's surface.

statement: Sound travels faster than light.
fact: Light travels at about 300,000 km/s, vastly faster than sound at roughly 343 m/s in air. That's why you see lightning before you hear thunder.

statement: Diamonds are formed from compressed coal.
fact: Most diamonds formed deep in the mantle, long before land plants existed to make coal. Both are simply made of carbon.

statement: Humans share about 60% of their DNA with bananas.
fact: Roughly 60% of human genes have recognizable counterparts in bananas, showing how much basic cell machinery all life shares.

statement: The human body has more bacterial cells than human cells.
fact: Newer estimates suggest the numbers are roughly equal, about 1:1. The older '10 to 1' claim was an overestimate.

statement: A hot object always has more heat energy than a cold one.
fact: Total thermal energy depends on mass and material as well as temperature. A huge iceberg holds more thermal energy than a hot cup of tea.

statement: Hot water can freeze faster than cold water under some conditions.
fact: This is called the Mpemba effect and has been observed in some experiments. Scientists still debate the exact causes.

statement: The Sun is yellow.
fact: The Sun emits all colors and is essentially white. It looks yellow from Earth because our atmosphere scatters blue light.

statement: Red blood in the human body turns blue when it has no oxygen.
fact: Deoxygenated blood is dark red. Veins look blue through the skin because of how light penetrates and scatters in tissue.

statement: Adults have fewer bones than babies.
fact: Babies are born with about 300 bones, many of which fuse as they grow. Adults have 206.

statement: Cracking your knuckles causes arthritis.
fact: Studies have found no link between knuckle cracking and arthritis. The popping sound comes from gas bubbles in the joint fluid.

statement: The chemical symbol for gold is Au.
fact: Au comes from the Latin word 'aurum' meaning gold.

statement: Antibiotics are effective against viral infections like the common cold.
fact: Antibiotics only kill bacteria. Using them for viruses does nothing and contributes to antibiotic resistance.

statement: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth.
fact: Sunlight travels roughly 150 million km and takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to arrive.

statement: Humans can survive without water for about three weeks.
fact: Most people can survive only about three days without water. It's food that people can go without for weeks.

statement: Camels store water in their humps.
fact: Camel humps store fat, which can be metabolized for energy. Camels conserve water through other adaptations.

statement: Dogs only see in black and white.
fact: Dogs see color, but mainly blues and yellows. They have two types of color receptors compared with three in humans.

statement: Dolphins are mammals.
fact: Dolphins breathe air, give birth to live young and nurse them with milk, all traits of mammals.

statement: A group of crows is called a murder.
fact: 'A murder of crows' is a traditional collective noun, likely inspired by folklore about the birds' ominous reputation.

statement: Spiders are insects.
fact: Spiders are arachnids with eight legs and two body segments. Insects have six legs and three body segments.

statement: Elephants are afraid of mice.
fact: There is no evidence that elephants fear mice. They may be startled by sudden movement, as many animals are.

statement: Koalas are a type of bear.
fact: Koalas are marsupials, not bears. They carry their young in a pouch like kangaroos.

statement: Cows have four stomachs.
fact: Cows have one stomach divided into four compartments. This setup lets them digest tough plant material through rumination.

statement: Penguins live at the North Pole.
fact: Penguins live almost exclusively in the Southern Hemisphere. Polar bears and other animals inhabit the Arctic.

statement: A shrimp's heart is located in its head.
fact: In shrimp, the heart sits in the thorax region of the head section. It is one of many quirks of crustacean anatomy.

statement: Blue whales are the largest animals known to have ever lived.
fact: Blue whales can reach about 30 meters in length and weigh up to 180 tonnes, larger than any known dinosaur.

statement: Chameleons change color mainly to blend into their surroundings.
fact: Color change is used mostly for communication and regulating temperature. Their natural coloring already provides camouflage.

statement: Sloths are among the fastest-moving mammals on land.
fact: Sloths are among the slowest mammals. Their low-energy diet of leaves keeps their metabolism very slow.

statement: Butterflies taste with their feet.
fact: Butterflies have taste receptors on their feet, which help them identify the right plants for laying eggs.

statement: Wolves howl at the Moon.
fact: Wolves howl to communicate with their pack and mark territory. The Moon has nothing to do with it.

statement: Starfish are classified as fish.
fact: Starfish, now often called sea stars, are echinoderms. They have no gills, scales or backbone.

statement: Hummingbirds can fly backwards.
fact: Hummingbirds can hover and fly backwards thanks to their unique wing rotation, a ability unmatched among birds.

statement: Touching a baby bird will make its mother abandon it.
fact: Most birds have a poor sense of smell and won't reject their chicks after human contact. Still, it is best to leave wildlife alone.

statement: The Great Fire of London took place in 1666.
fact: The fire destroyed about 13,000 houses and much of the medieval city, yet only a handful of deaths were officially recorded.

statement: The Titanic sank on its maiden voyage.
fact: RMS Titanic struck an iceberg and sank in April 1912 during its first trip from Southampton to New York.

statement: Vikings wore horned helmets in battle.
fact: There's no evidence Vikings wore horned helmets. The image was popularized by 19th-century costume designs for operas.

statement: Marie Antoinette said 'Let them eat cake.'
fact: There is no record she ever said it. The phrase appeared in writings before she arrived in France and was attributed to her later.

statement: The pyramids of Giza were built by slaves.
fact: Archaeological evidence points to paid laborers who were housed, fed and given burial near the pyramids.

statement: World War I began in 1914.
fact: The war began after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria in June 1914, and fighting escalated that summer.

statement: Albert Einstein failed math in school.
fact: Einstein excelled at math and had mastered calculus by about 15. The myth likely arose from a misunderstanding about a grading system change.

statement: The Berlin Wall fell in 1989.
fact: The wall that divided East and West Berlin was opened on November 9, 1989, and Germany reunified in 1990.

statement: Christopher Columbus set out to prove the Earth was round.
fact: Educated Europeans already knew the Earth was round. The real debate was about the distance to Asia, which Columbus badly underestimated.

statement: The Hundred Years' War lasted exactly 100 years.
fact: The conflict between England and France lasted 116 years, from 1337 to 1453.

statement: Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire.
fact: Teaching at Oxford existed by 1096, while the Aztec city of Tenochtitlan was founded in 1325.

statement: Medieval people believed the Earth was flat.
fact: Scholars in the Middle Ages understood the Earth was spherical. The flat-Earth myth was largely popularized in the 19th century.

statement: The Roman Colosseum was used for gladiator fights.
fact: The Colosseum hosted gladiator contests, animal hunts and public spectacles for crowds of roughly 50,000 people.

statement: Mahatma Gandhi won the Nobel Peace Prize.
fact: Gandhi was nominated several times but never won. The Nobel Committee later publicly expressed regret over the omission.

statement: The Declaration of Independence was signed on July 4, 1776 by all delegates.
fact: July 4 is when the text was adopted, but most delegates signed on August 2, 1776, and others signed later.

statement: The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo da Vinci.
fact: Leonardo painted it in the early 1500s, and it now hangs in the Louvre in Paris.

statement: Nepal is the birthplace of Gautama Buddha.
fact: Siddhartha Gautama was born in Lumbini, in present-day Nepal, around the 6th century BCE.

statement: The first Harry Potter book is titled 'Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets'.
fact: The first book is 'Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone' (Sorcerer's Stone in the US). The Chamber of Secrets is the second.

statement: Darth Vader says 'Luke, I am your father' in The Empire Strikes Back.
fact: The actual line is 'No, I am your father.' The popular misquote has become more famous than the real one.

statement: Mario, the Nintendo character, was originally called Jumpman.
fact: He first appeared as 'Jumpman' in the 1981 arcade game Donkey Kong, and was later renamed Mario.

statement: The Beatles were from Liverpool, England.
fact: John, Paul, George and Ringo all came from Liverpool, where the band formed in 1960.

statement: In Pac-Man, the ghosts are named Inky, Blinky, Pinky and Clyde.
fact: The four ghosts each have different movement behaviors, which makes the game's patterns more strategic than they appear.

statement: Sherlock Holmes never actually says 'Elementary, my dear Watson' in the original Conan Doyle stories.
fact: The famous phrase never appears in that exact form in the original books. It became popular through later films and adaptations.

statement: The movie Titanic won 11 Academy Awards.
fact: Titanic tied the record for most Oscar wins, matching Ben-Hur and later The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King.

statement: Michael Jackson's 'Thriller' is the best-selling album of all time.
fact: Released in 1982, Thriller is estimated to have sold over 70 million copies worldwide.

statement: The video game Minecraft was created by Mojang's founder Markus 'Notch' Persson.
fact: Notch released an early version in 2009, and Microsoft later bought Mojang in 2014 for about $2.5 billion.

statement: The Simpsons is the longest-running American animated TV series.
fact: The show premiered as a series in 1989 and has aired for more than three decades.

statement: Bollywood is the name of the Indian film industry based in Chennai.
fact: Bollywood refers to the Hindi-language film industry based in Mumbai. Chennai is known for Tamil cinema, sometimes called Kollywood.

statement: The first iPhone was released in 2007.
fact: Steve Jobs introduced the original iPhone in January 2007, and it went on sale that June.

statement: In the game of chess, the queen is the most powerful piece.
fact: The queen can move any number of squares in any direction, combining the moves of a rook and a bishop.

statement: Humans have 46 chromosomes in most body cells.
fact: Humans normally have 23 pairs of chromosomes, totaling 46, in each body cell.

statement: A leap year occurs every 4 years without exception.
fact: Century years like 1900 are not leap years unless divisible by 400. That is why 2000 was a leap year but 1900 was not.

statement: There are 12 months in the Gregorian calendar that have 31 days.
fact: Only seven months have 31 days: January, March, May, July, August, October and December.

statement: Roman numeral 'M' represents 1,000.
fact: M comes from the Latin 'mille', meaning thousand, and is the largest standard single Roman numeral.

statement: Left-handed people make up about 10% of the world's population.
fact: Roughly one in ten people are left-handed, a proportion that has stayed remarkably consistent across cultures.

statement: The Olympic Games originated in ancient Greece.
fact: The ancient Olympics were held at Olympia starting in 776 BCE, and the modern Games were revived in 1896.

statement: You lose most of your body heat through your head.
fact: The head loses about as much heat as any other uncovered body part per area. The myth came from a flawed military study that kept the rest of the body covered.

statement: Mount Everest is located on the border of Nepal and China (Tibet).
fact: The summit sits on the border between Nepal and the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.
